items.summary: Memory enables language agents to carry useful distinctions from past experience into future decisions. Its value depends on which distinctions survive, whether a bounded agent can use them, and what can be recovered or revised as demands evolve. We develop a decision-theoretic framework that follows this value from raw history through persistent state, operational use, and costly recovery and revision. Original and retained value are expressed in units of avoided task loss; risk-cost frontiers describe attainable recovery and preservation across uses. Unknown demand yields value profiles, while interactive feedback changes the distribution of future work. A cost-aware simulation condition and five minimal counterexamples expose the roles of information timing, retrieval access, component interaction, feedback and demand uncertainty. In particular, a pointer with zero mutual information about the answer can still reduce the cost of exact recovery. Diagnostics on LoCoMo, a two-project update task and longitudinal cases exhibit failures of preservation, use and measurement. At fixed retrieved evidence, a saved ledger changes subsequent answers; at fixed agent outputs, an evaluator revision changes scores. The framework connects these distinctions to operational risk bounds and testable principles for allocating memory, preserving recovery options and revising evidence dependencies.
items.title: The Value of Memory in Language Agents

items.summary: We study intermediate sample-size efficiency for censored regression tests when the signal and significance level both tend to zero. Independent treatment assignment permits finite-sample conditional sign calibration under arbitrary outcome dependence. For stationary ergodic latent fields with independent smooth site noise, bounded scores learned from the same pooled outcomes retain their first-order drift under empirical squared-error consistency, without an estimation-rate requirement. An observable censored rank procedure consequently admits an explicit leading cost on long-range dependent fields with nonsummable covariances. Smooth response scores admit a complementary result without independent site noise. For observational fields, separated blocks and paired variance calibration control the dependence approximation at the nominal testing level and yield sample-size costs under explicit absolute-regularity envelopes. An exactly centered censored contrast removes unknown marginal centering under stated exogeneity conditions. We also give a product-limit construction for independent random censoring, information-loss identities, and directional score-bank comparisons. Numerical studies distinguish procedure loss, score-learning loss, and spatial variance inflation. A stationary nonergodic counterexample and an uncensored Gaussian benchmark delimit the field results. Independent-data proofs, finite-range constructions, and a finite-dimensional measurement extension are included in the same manuscript.
tags: censored regression; intermediate efficiency; long-range dependence; random field; randomization tes
items.title: Intermediate efficiency of censored regression tests on stationary random fields

items.summary: Differential Privacy (DP) has become a prominent approach for protecting graph data releases, yet empirical auditing methodologies have largely been developed for tabular datasets and machine learning pipelines rather than graph-structured outputs. We present a methodology for empirically auditing DP graph release mechanisms, identifying two graph-specific audit design problems: canary construction and witness statistic selection. We combine these components with an established statistically certified testing procedure and implement the resulting methodology as an open-source Python toolkit. To demonstrate the approach, we audit a published state-of-the-art Node-DP graph release mechanism. Across a series of synthetic and real-world canary pairs, we obtain certified lower bounds on the privacy parameter {\varepsilon} that exceed the claimed value, yielding counterexamples sufficient to falsify the claimed guarantee for the audited implementation. The violations persist under progressively stronger restrictions on the input domain, including non-empty and connected graphs. We also show that witness selection can materially affect whether a violation is detected, highlighting the importance of evaluating a diverse battery of statistics when auditing DP graph release mechanisms.
items.title: Practical Auditing of Differentially Private Graph Release Mechanisms: Methodology, Toolkit, and Case Study

items.summary: Overview This software package accompanies the study Resolvability of Ionospheric Currents From Multi-LEO Magnetometry . It provides computational tools for investigating how multi-altitude satellite magnetic observations constrain three-dimensional ionospheric currents. The package implements a divergence-free spherical Mie magnetic-field representation and a Bayesian inversion framework for evaluating magnetic-field and current reconstruction, degrees of freedom for signal (DFS), physical-current information, and posterior uncertainty. Main Features Spherical-harmonic Mie forward modeling and three-component current reconstruction. Bayesian inversion with full posterior covariance propagation. Resolution and recoverability diagnostics for different satellite configurations and observation altitudes. Physical-current information analysis and regularization-sensitivity experiments. Synthetic current-recovery experiments, calibration routines, and figure-generation workflows. Python and optional MATLAB implementations, with independent numerical verification. Sample Swarm-A/B orbital positions for geometry tests and a self-contained synthetic inversion example. What's New in This Version 3 This release provides a corrected scientific implementation and updated reproducibility tools. The principal corrections include: Correcting the colatitude derivative of the associated Legendre functions used in the spherical-harmonic operator. Restoring the radial magnetic-field contribution of the quadratic poloidal Mie term, ensuring consistency with the continuous divergence-free representation. Updating the corresponding current-reconstruction and recoverability calculations. Clarifying the scaled coefficient parameterization, Bayesian prior, and interpretation of coefficient-space resolution diagnostics. Improving numerical verification, reproducibility workflows, and documentation. The updated calculations continue to support the importance of satellite altitude separation for constraining specified ionospheric current structures, while distinguishing formal information gain from recovery of the complete physical current distribution. Data and Reproducibility The package includes source code, documentation, numerical tests, small reference summaries, sample orbit positions, and a self-contained synthetic example. The synthetic demonstrations can be executed without downloading mission magnetic-field observations. Reproducing the study's observation-based analyses requires the corresponding processed Swarm and Macau Science Satellite-1 data and additional external inputs described in the documentation. Large intermediate numerical archives and original magnetic observation records are not redistributed in this software package. Citation and License Please cite the version-specific Zenodo DOI and the software authors listed in CITATION.cff when using this package. Author-owned software and documentation are distributed under the MIT License. Included spacecraft-derived orbit excerpts and external datasets remain subject to their respective data-provider terms. This release supersedes the previous software implementation while retaining earlier versions in the same Zenodo version history.
items.title: Resolvability of Ionospheric Currents From Multi-LEO Magnetometry: Software and Reproducibility Package

items.summary: Anaxia, the BLLM engine: typed construction search, independent checks and recorded failure residues. This research candidate adds twelve exact finite-interval certificates for reflexive four-polytopes, an independent integer verifier, and a portable animated certificate explorer. Relative to the supplied Kreuzer–Skarke point-pair census, the maximum shortest descent satisfies 22 ≤ D4 ≤ 346. The prior bound 348 for arbitrary descents is unchanged. The verifier reconstructs facets, primal and polar lattice points, strict containment, interval costs, pair bounds and exceptional-census coverage. It does not reconstruct the entire classification histogram. The sharp seed constant, Hodge F2/F3-prime, GSC and the continuum Yang–Mills problem remain open. The full four-target closure benchmark has not been crossed. Graph survivors are necessary candidate configurations, not constructed semiregular objects. No new Lean formalization of the interval refinement is claimed.
items.title: BLLM: Beyond the LLM with Deep Human-Mind-AI

items.summary: Background : The rapid digitisation of allied health education has led to an alarming rise in Digital Eye Strain (DES), also termed Computer Vision Syndrome (CVS), among undergraduate Bachelor of Physiotherapy (BPT) students. Standard therapies like artificial tears provide temporary lubrication without resolving the underlying neuro-vascular tension and oxidative ocular stress. Objectives : To evaluate and compare the therapeutic efficacy of daily Isotonic Saline Jal Neti versus Sterile Triphala Water Eye Wash over 4 weeks on digital asthenopia, tear film stability, tear volume, and visual comfort in a cohort of 16 BPT students. Methodology : A 4-week prospective, parallel-group, randomized controlled empirical pilot trial was conducted at Maya Devi University, Dehradun. Sixteen BPT students (aged 18–25) meeting inclusion criteria (screen time ≥ 6 hrs/day, CVS-Q ≥ 6, TBUT < 10 s) were randomized 1:1 into Group A (Jal Neti, n=8) and Group B (Sterile Triphala Water Eye Wash, n=8). Outcome metrics assessed at baseline (Day 0) and post-intervention (Day 28) included: Computer Vision Syndrome Questionnaire (CVS-Q), Visual Fatigue Scale (VFS, 0-60), Tear Break-Up Time (TBUT, seconds), and Schirmer’s Test-I (mm/5 min). Results : Both groups exhibited statistically significant intra-group improvements across all parameters (p < 0.001). Group B (Triphala) achieved superior improvement in tear film stability and lacrimal secretion: TBUT increased by +4.15 ± 0.80 s in Group B vs. +2.30 ± 0.60 s in Group A (p < 0.001); Schirmer-I values increased by +4.85 ± 1.10 mm in Group B vs. +2.65 ± 0.85 mm in Group A (p < 0.001). Conversely, Group A (Jal Neti) achieved greater relief from central visual fatigue and periocular headaches: VFS scores decreased by -18.60 ± 2.95 points in Group A vs. -14.25 ± 2.75 points in Group B (p < 0.01). Total CVS-Q scores dropped markedly in both groups (Group A: 12.75 to 5.25; Group B: 13.00 to 4.90). Conclusion : Both modalities significantly alleviate digital eye strain in BPT students. Sterile Triphala eye wash is particularly potent for restoring ocular surface hydration and tear film stability, whereas Jal Neti excels in alleviating deep neuromuscular fatigue and periorbital strain.
tags: Digital Eye Strain, Jal Neti, Triphala, Tear Break-Up Time, Schirmer's Test, Physiotherapy Students,
items.title: Comparative Evaluation of Isotonic Saline Jal Neti versus Sterile Triphala Water Eye Wash on Digital Asthenopia, Tear Film Dynamics, and Visual Comfort in Undergraduate Physiotherapy Students: A Single-Center Empirical Pilot Study

items.summary: In this article, we use the PBNF-transform, or Polynomial Boolean Normal Form, described earlier in two articles and now extended to higher arity, to solve Boolean satisfiability problems (SAT), which are part of the P versus NP problem. SAT consists of a statement of conjunctions of clauses, and in our SAT-solving models, we dualize the logical equations, inverting the problem by \emph{multiplying} letters (literals) in the transferred clauses, now phrases: $pqrs\cdots s_{\ell}$, and using a binary iterated composition based on \emph{adding polynomials} for the conjunctions in our solution formula. We obtain Polynomial Boolean Equations, PBE=0, by also renaming the truth value $1\mapsto 0$(T). To find a solution, we look for repeating literals in the clauses to factor out. With reversed literal repetition, we can even reduce the CNF to the sum of the transformed clauses.
items.title: A Study in Solution Models for SAT using the PBNF-transform

items.summary: Generative AI is widely framed as democratizing skilled work by lowering the barrier to producing professional output. Drawing on 21 semi-structured interviews with 27 workers across 21 small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) in Kenya and Nigeria (July to October 2023), we find that availability alone did not make participation workable. In participants' accounts, drafting was rarely the hard part. The consequential work was making AI-assisted drafts defensible enough to circulate to clients. We identify five intertwined practices through which participants made generative AI workable: using it as draft labour, steering outputs through iterative interaction, switching and comparing across tools, performing release work to make outputs accountable before circulation, and repairing context misfit when outputs failed local requirements. We make two central contributions. First, we specify release work as a distinct, boundary-facing form of accountability labour, evidenced through verification gates, traceability reconstruction when sources fail, and non-delegation boundaries that decide what can ship. Second, we show how localization and representational failures, which we call context misfit, operate in everyday work as a recurring breakdown-and-repair class, including failures of local language, institutional knowledge, and the credible representation of African people and places, and we document the repair repertoire they demanded. Reframing democratization as workable participation, we argue that reported gains were conditional on this accountability and repair labour, and we translate the findings into four design directions for workplace generative AI. We treat Kenya and Nigeria as two situated cases, not as a representative sample of SMBs or the Global South.
items.title: Making Generative AI Workable at Work: Accountability, Localization, and Representation in Kenyan and Nigerian Small Businesses

items.summary: Companion Lean 4 formalization and computational verification materials for Yunkun Song's manuscript "Pattern-avoiding binary arrays and a Stirling-type table: explicit formulas, exact recurrence orders, and non-D-finiteness" (OEIS A207123). The archive contains 80 Lean modules with a pinned Lean 4/Mathlib v4.34.1 toolchain, verification scripts (414 automated checks in 14 modules), supporting notes, input snapshots, historical verification logs, and the corresponding manuscript. Manuscript Section 9 maps results to formal theorem names and describes the scope of formalization. This deposit freezes source revision 7ced433fadc1ca3dedced4e0d2fdce4032f7d5e5 of the previously published repository. It is independently downloadable without access to that GitHub account. See ARCHIVE_README.md for entry points, reproduction instructions, provenance, and the checks performed in preparing this deposit. The full Lean compilation and 414-check suite were not rerun for the deposit. Licensing is mixed and unchanged: code is MIT licensed; the manuscript, report, notes and other text are excluded and remain all rights reserved; OEIS snapshots retain CC BY-SA 4.0 and attribution; other third-party data retains its original terms. See the included LICENSE and NOTICE files.

items.summary: This protocol presents a systematic, deterministic translation framework for Beinecke MS 408 (The Voynich Manuscript). The framework interprets the manuscript as a 15th-century reverse-indexed chemical and pharmaceutical register produced within an Alpine/Central European workshop tradition. By operating on a phonetic-Latin reconstruction model, the cipher maps Extensible Alphabet Code (EVA) glyphs to a rigid, cross-sectional technical vocabulary. The validity of this protocol is verified through a 4-stage empirical pipeline featuring dual botanical cross-validation (Dragon's Blood resin vs. Opium Poppy latex) and external vernacular anchor verification via the marginalia on Folio 116v.
items.title: Voynich Manuscript Final Decoding Procedure

items.summary: Conformance vectors for agent execution evidence, and the reference verifier that judges them. This release carries 39 corpus manifests across 38 suites and 2,154 vectors in all, among them the in-toto adversarial-execution-evidence predicate, the in-toto ai-agent-action predicate, an AI generation predicate, the observed-effect predicate, SCITT COSE carriage, signed decision receipts and receipt chains, an anchor-stream verifier, ACS core, artifact binding, MCP response-phase interception, the OWASP MCP verification draft, the W3C per-check reporting format and intake, A2A agent-card canonicalization, delegation lifecycle, authority at dispatch, done contracts and receipts, grader isolation, spoofed tool output, test tampering, and ACI deployments. One binary judges every one of them, selected by the suite each corpus manifest declares. Each corpus digest is listed, recomputed from the vector files, in CORPUS-DIGESTS.txt, which the GitHub release signs and timestamps. The predicate's model is execute-and-attest rather than match-and-assert: a consumer recomputes the outcome from the bytes the statement carries, instead of trusting a verdict the producer asserted about itself. This repository is a second, independently usable implementation of that contract, so that any producer of the predicate type can self-certify and any consumer can reject a lying emitter. For the adversarial-execution-evidence corpus this deposit covers suite revision 32: 288 vectors, of which 63 accept, 223 reject and 2 are indeterminate. Its bytes are fixed by the corpus digest bf3e5befd71640757ff1b3f0af63507364b823b5e3f9059678f72f64a46e11c1 recorded in vectors/MANIFEST.json. A published revision is never mutated in place; a normative change to the predicate, or an addition to the corpus, bumps the revision and regenerates every vector byte-identically from its generators, because the vendored specification's digest is itself a corpus input. The archive is the output of git archive --format=tar.gz --prefix=agent-evidence-vectors-0.25.0/ v0.25.0 and reproduces byte for byte from the signed tag (SHA-256 ffd80cc752769d69ef13745f55cac9ab99d5a3cd5476f19359c2646597290970). The intended use is citation by a conformance requirement. A requirement that names this suite, or any other suite demonstrated to exercise the same conditions, is checkable by a party who trusts neither the producer nor the implementer. Cite this version DOI for a conformance claim; the concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22758687 always resolves to the newest release.
items.title: agent-evidence-vectors: conformance vectors for agent execution evidence

items.summary: Reproducible Python/Colab pipeline that processes ECOSTRESS L2T LSTE v002 land surface temperature (70 m) to detect closed depressions acting as cold-air traps in the Central Middle Atlas (Morocco): local LST anomaly against a 5 km background, morphological reconstruction of closed depressions, D8 cold-air flow routing without depression filling, a harmonic model of nocturnal inversion development, statistical determinants, robustness and between-period stability.
items.title: caps-ecostress-moyen-atlas: detection of cold-air pools from ECOSTRESS nocturnal land surface temperature and terrain morphology

items.summary: Diffusion models have become strong priors for solving inverse problems. However, nonlinear inverse problems such as phase retrieval remain challenging when multiple measurement-consistent solutions are distinguishable only by the prior; we call such measurements ambiguous. Existing diffusion-based samplers rely on local approximations during reconstruction. For an ambiguous measurement, these approximations can allow measurement guidance to favor a measurement-consistent mode that is close to a prior-supported mode but is itself not supported by the prior. Evaluation often masks this type of failure by reporting the best-of-$k$ runs, where the best is selected by comparison to the ground truth. We introduce Prior-Consistent DAPS (PC-DAPS), a variant of Decoupled Annealing Posterior Sampling (DAPS) designed to address this failure case by maintaining multiple candidate solutions within a single sampling run. As annealing noise decreases, PC-DAPS prunes and replaces weaker candidates according to their prior consistency, without any ground-truth access. PC-DAPS reduces the incidence of prior-inconsistent samples and improves sample quality on nonlinear inverse problems while preserving sample quality and diversity on linear inverse problems.
items.title: Beyond Best-of-$k$: Prior-Consistent DAPS for Ambiguous Nonlinear Inverse Problems

items.summary: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) enable flexible masked generation through bidirectional context modeling, but this capability also introduces a distinct jailbreak attack surface. We find that a harmful response to a given query naturally serves as an effective jailbreak template: simply masking a subset of its tokens can induce a dLLM to reconstruct harmful content. Based on this observation, we propose RMT-Jailbreak, a general framework that transfers existing autoregressive (AR) jailbreak attacks to dLLMs through their induced harmful responses. RMT-Jailbreak converts an AR-generated harmful response into a high-mask-ratio template using uniform token retention, and further applies prompt-based safety filtering to mask any remaining visible harmful content. The refined template is then provided to the target dLLM for bidirectional reconstruction. Extensive experiments across multiple AR jailbreak methods and target dLLMs demonstrate the effectiveness and generality of RMT-Jailbreak, revealing strong cross-paradigm transferability of jailbreak attacks.
items.title: Harmful Responses Are Jailbreak Templates: Transferring Autoregressive Jailbreaks to Diffusion Language Models

items.summary: Abstract: Artificial intelligence increasingly mediates game production and player participation, but claims about game merging frequently conflate different technical achievements. This article examines AI game melding as the convergence of agent-assisted reconstruction, executable interoperability, and creative recombination. An integrative narrative review connects procedural generation, computational blending, modding, co-creation, and decompilation research with public documentation available through October 15, 2026. Cases include meme-based and Wii Sports crossovers in World at War Zombies, a Call of Duty and Minecraft hybrid, runtime bridging, and agent-assisted reconstruction. The analysis separates creator demonstrations and reported acceleration from independently validated performance. It proposes a five-layer composability stack comprising representation, semantics, runtime, verification, and permission. Reduced implementation friction may relocate production bottlenecks, making behavioral validation, design coherence, maintenance, and rights governance increasingly consequential. Four conditional scenarios are considered: expanded bespoke play, abundance accompanied by discoverability problems, stronger enclosure, and governed experimentation. The literature gap concerns limited integrated evidence linking substantial game reconstruction and interoperability to community, economic, and governance outcomes, rather than an absence of earlier blending research. Proposed studies address acceleration, player experience, attribution, preservation, and platform power. Game melding may redistribute creative authority, but its consequences depend on institutions and verification practices surrounding programmable play rather than technical capability alone.
tags: generative artificial intelligence; game melding; modding; decompilation; human-AI co-creation; plat
items.title: AI Game Melding: Agent-Assisted Reconstruction, Player Co-Creation, and the Future of Programmable Play

items.summary: Many LLM agents maintain external persistent memory and derive additional state from past interactions, such as summaries. Deleting an original memory record therefore need not remove information carried by its descendants. We introduce AfterDeleteBench, a controlled behavioral audit for this failure mode in fixed-weight LLM agents. For each synthetic secret, we compare an exposed-then-deleted agent with an otherwise matched agent that was never exposed to the secret, allowing post-deletion recovery to be attributed to the original exposure. In our primary setting, a single query recovers the deleted secret from Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct in roughly two thirds of cases, while matched never-exposed controls have zero recovery. Crucially, recovery does not require a surviving verbatim copy: when the complete secret string is absent and only separately stored components remain under a public composition rule, exact reconstruction succeeds in 62-99% of cases across Qwen, Mistral, and Phi-3. We also show that the response interface is part of the measurement system: target-bearing replies can be scored as failures when the requested format and parser are misaligned. Finally, we separate reconstruction from write-back and fresh-session recall. Provenance-aware closure eliminates observed recovery in the tested positive-baseline settings, whereas an exact-literal write filter blocks reinsertion but cannot erase information already present. Together, these results show that source deletion should be evaluated behaviorally at the level of the agent and its memory system, not only as a storage operation.
items.title: AfterDeleteBench: Auditing Post-Deletion Information Persistence in LLM Agents

items.summary: We envision a general-purpose protein foundation model as a unified, interactive model of sequence, structure, and function, capable of understanding, generation, and cross-modal translation while retaining the instruction-following and reasoning capabilities of modern LLMs. Toward this vision, we introduce Trion-1, the first native, unified, multimodal diffusion language model (dLLM) for proteins. Trion-1 is built on two key design choices: (1) a unified discrete token space that jointly represents sequence, structure, and natural language; (2) a dLLM backbone that replaces strict left-to-right factorization with bidirectional or semi-bidirectional token interactions, enabling global residue communication and long-range contact modeling that are naturally suited to structure modeling. This formulation unifies six core capabilities: folding, inverse folding, sequence understanding, structure understanding, sequence design, and structure design, while retaining the native language capabilities of general-purpose LLMs. On established benchmarks, Trion-1 achieves broadly competitive performance. In folding, Trion-1 achieves a TM-score above 0.8 with a single sample under strict homology control, matching or exceeding the existing tri-modal model using 200 samples. For sequence understanding, Trion-1 performs on par with top-tier LLMs such as Claude Opus 4.7 (62.37%). These results support well-aligned sequence-structure-language representations and strong cross-modal generative capabilities.
items.title: Trion-1: Unifying Language, Protein Sequence, and Structure with Diffusion Language Models

items.summary: This paper develops the Phase Compatibility branch of Harmonic Physics: a framework for examining how physical participants enter constrained phase relations, produce collective outcomes, and form persistent higher-level organisations capable of further recursive participation. Building on established synchronization theory, phase locking, coupled-oscillator dynamics and phasor mathematics, the framework examines reinforcement, opposition, cancellation, reshaping and whole formation. It distinguishes mathematical admissibility, actual source occupancy, participant admission, active interaction, closure, continuing identity and observation. A compatibility basin is characterised through maintained relational organisation and persistence under declared conditions. Version 3.1 aligns the shared definitions with the current Foundations and Observer Theory papers, corrects the amplitude-weighted moment family, and clarifies the distinction between passive changes of representation and physical projection or coupling. It incorporates the completed mathematical nesting construction, which preserves a supplied quantum state’s amplitude and relative-phase information, together with Born probabilities under corresponding joint measurements. Phase Theory Equations is identified as the consolidated reference for the current mathematical expressions. The observation account separates source organisation, information encoded into light, receiver coupling, registration, retention and calibrated reconstruction. Within the proposed optical terminology, light performs the observer role through source–receiver coupling, while the receiver registers and retains a physical response. Minimal relational consciousness and awareness retain separate definitions. The paper integrates controlled models, molecular spectral studies, a superconducting-qubit analogue, simulated liquid-water reorganisation, quantum-state encoding and specified receiver models, preserving the scope and limitations of each result. It sets out the state spaces, conservation requirements, comparison models and prospective failure conditions required for physical applications. Universal participant-admission and whole-formation laws remain open research questions; this revision introduces no new experimental validation.
items.title: Phase Compatibility: Harmonic Combination, Selective Participation, Whole Formation, and Recursive Organisation

items.summary: Memory enables language agents to carry useful distinctions from past experience into future decisions. Its value depends on which distinctions survive, whether a bounded agent can use them, and what can be recovered or revised as demands evolve. We develop a decision-theoretic framework that follows this value from raw history through persistent state, operational use, and costly recovery and revision. Original and retained value are expressed in units of avoided task loss; risk-cost frontiers describe attainable recovery and preservation across uses. Unknown demand yields value profiles, while interactive feedback changes the distribution of future work. A cost-aware simulation condition and five minimal counterexamples expose the roles of information timing, retrieval access, component interaction, feedback and demand uncertainty. In particular, a pointer with zero mutual information about the answer can still reduce the cost of exact recovery. Diagnostics on LoCoMo, a two-project update task and longitudinal cases exhibit failures of preservation, use and measurement. At fixed retrieved evidence, a saved ledger changes subsequent answers; at fixed agent outputs, an evaluator revision changes scores. The framework connects these distinctions to operational risk bounds and testable principles for allocating memory, preserving recovery options and revising evidence dependencies.
items.title: The Value of Memory in Language Agents

items.summary: Anaxia, the BLLM engine: typed construction search, independent checks and recorded failure residues. This research candidate adds twelve exact finite-interval certificates for reflexive four-polytopes, an independent integer verifier, and a portable animated certificate explorer. Relative to the supplied Kreuzer–Skarke point-pair census, the maximum shortest descent satisfies 22 ≤ D4 ≤ 346. The prior bound 348 for arbitrary descents is unchanged. The verifier reconstructs facets, primal and polar lattice points, strict containment, interval costs, pair bounds and exceptional-census coverage. It does not reconstruct the entire classification histogram. The sharp seed constant, Hodge F2/F3-prime, GSC and the continuum Yang–Mills problem remain open. The full four-target closure benchmark has not been crossed. Graph survivors are necessary candidate configurations, not constructed semiregular objects. No new Lean formalization of the interval refinement is claimed.
items.title: BLLM: Beyond the LLM with Deep Human-Mind-AI

items.summary: Prediction intervals from probabilistic time-series forecasters are commonly assessed by marginal coverage, the long-run proportion of observations falling inside the intervals. However, forecast errors in time series are often serially dependent and heteroskedastic, so prediction intervals can attain near-nominal marginal coverage while miscovering systematically during periods of larger local error variance. We identify and address this failure mode, which we call \emph{local scale miscalibration}. We first document the phenomenon using time-series foundation models (TSFMs): across several real-world series, their native intervals often attain near-nominal marginal coverage while exhibiting substantial temporal variation in local coverage, alternating between overcoverage and undercoverage over shorter windows. We then propose Volatility-Corrected Prediction Intervals (VCPI), a post-hoc calibration procedure that uses the base forecaster's predictive scale as a baseline, models the volatility of standardized forecast residuals with a Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity (GARCH) model, and applies a multiplicative correction to produce locally adaptive prediction intervals. We justify VCPI both theoretically and empirically, comparing it against model-agnostic conformal counterparts. We provide a theoretical analysis of interval adaptation of the proposed method following abrupt changes in volatility. Empirically, we evaluate VCPI on Chronos, Moirai, and TimesFM across four real-world datasets and find that it produces more stable local coverage than conformal baselines while maintaining near-nominal marginal coverage and comparable interval width.
items.title: Volatility-Corrected Prediction Intervals: Locally Adaptive Uncertainty Quantification for Probabilistic Time-Series Forecasting

items.summary: Code, frozen configurations, input data, outputs and logs behind the Working sheet for MQG v0.3.8: chiral active Model H in three dimensions — computational validation addendum (MQG: magnetic quorum gravity). The archive contains the pre-registered canonical fit (v1.0), the frozen v1.1 analysis (angular torque test; joint fit with mixed noise), a reproduction on separate hardware, a second-algorithm check, and frozen acceptance tolerances for a future independent fitter. A SHA-256 manifest of every file is included. Interpretation level 1. All dispersion data are synthetic; the results verify software, uncertainty calibration and parameter identifiability, not the physics. The canonical fit v1.0 passes 15 of 16 pre-registered criteria and the v1.1 analysis passes 9 of 10; both failures stay on record. A pre-registered fit by an independent implementer is still open. The author independently reviewed the cited sources, equations, numerical procedures, computational results, scientific interpretations and final claims, and accepts full responsibility for the content. AI-assisted output was not treated as evidence, and computational verification was evaluated separately from physical evidence.
items.title: Code, frozen configurations, input data, outputs and logs behind the MQG v0.3.8 working sheet

items.summary: In standard acoustic anomaly detection (ASD), models are usually trained separately for each machine or domain using explicit metadata. However, in realistic deployments, machine identifiers are incomplete, unreliable, or simply unavailable. Thus, metadata-free machinery ASD asks a single model to monitor mixed machine populations without machine IDs. In this paper, we argue that the main failure mode is not a weak detector family, but representation entanglement. The heterogeneous normal modes overlap in frozen pre-trained feature spaces, making anomaly scoring and approximate retrieval unreliable. We study this problem directly and propose HARMONY (Hierarchical Anchor Retrieval on Manifold for Oblivious-source acoustic aNomalY detection), an anchor-guided geometric repartitioning framework that reorganizes mixed-source features into compact Voronoi regions and reuses this structure for hierarchical retrieval. On DCASE 2020, HARMONY improves mean AUC from 75.40% to 90.00% (14.60 percentage points) over the strongest unified baseline and from 83.90% to 90.00% over a strong foundation-feature baseline. On a single CPU, its hierarchical retrieval achieves a 7.8x speedup over exhaustive search with only a 0.20 percentage-point AUC drop. These results suggest that incorporating explicit geometric partitioning can improve both detection accuracy and retrieval efficiency for ASD. Code is available at https://github.com/Zzyh0208/HARMONY.
items.title: HARMONY: Hierarchical Anchor Retrieval on Manifold for Oblivious-source Machinery Acoustic Anomaly Detection

items.summary: Many LLM agents maintain external persistent memory and derive additional state from past interactions, such as summaries. Deleting an original memory record therefore need not remove information carried by its descendants. We introduce AfterDeleteBench, a controlled behavioral audit for this failure mode in fixed-weight LLM agents. For each synthetic secret, we compare an exposed-then-deleted agent with an otherwise matched agent that was never exposed to the secret, allowing post-deletion recovery to be attributed to the original exposure. In our primary setting, a single query recovers the deleted secret from Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct in roughly two thirds of cases, while matched never-exposed controls have zero recovery. Crucially, recovery does not require a surviving verbatim copy: when the complete secret string is absent and only separately stored components remain under a public composition rule, exact reconstruction succeeds in 62-99% of cases across Qwen, Mistral, and Phi-3. We also show that the response interface is part of the measurement system: target-bearing replies can be scored as failures when the requested format and parser are misaligned. Finally, we separate reconstruction from write-back and fresh-session recall. Provenance-aware closure eliminates observed recovery in the tested positive-baseline settings, whereas an exact-literal write filter blocks reinsertion but cannot erase information already present. Together, these results show that source deletion should be evaluated behaviorally at the level of the agent and its memory system, not only as a storage operation.
items.title: AfterDeleteBench: Auditing Post-Deletion Information Persistence in LLM Agents

items.summary: Generative AI is widely framed as democratizing skilled work by lowering the barrier to producing professional output. Drawing on 21 semi-structured interviews with 27 workers across 21 small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) in Kenya and Nigeria (July to October 2023), we find that availability alone did not make participation workable. In participants' accounts, drafting was rarely the hard part. The consequential work was making AI-assisted drafts defensible enough to circulate to clients. We identify five intertwined practices through which participants made generative AI workable: using it as draft labour, steering outputs through iterative interaction, switching and comparing across tools, performing release work to make outputs accountable before circulation, and repairing context misfit when outputs failed local requirements. We make two central contributions. First, we specify release work as a distinct, boundary-facing form of accountability labour, evidenced through verification gates, traceability reconstruction when sources fail, and non-delegation boundaries that decide what can ship. Second, we show how localization and representational failures, which we call context misfit, operate in everyday work as a recurring breakdown-and-repair class, including failures of local language, institutional knowledge, and the credible representation of African people and places, and we document the repair repertoire they demanded. Reframing democratization as workable participation, we argue that reported gains were conditional on this accountability and repair labour, and we translate the findings into four design directions for workplace generative AI. We treat Kenya and Nigeria as two situated cases, not as a representative sample of SMBs or the Global South.
items.title: Making Generative AI Workable at Work: Accountability, Localization, and Representation in Kenyan and Nigerian Small Businesses

items.summary: Large language models have shown outstanding performance on text-first tasks such as coding, math, and writing. Recent efforts are shifting models' training to include scientific problems that often live in highly specialized domains beyond text, such as protein structure and biological images. However, in these scenarios, their general-purpose accuracy compared with specialized algorithms remains in question. One such domain is cell tracking, which requires spatiotemporal awareness of cell dynamics. To evaluate this, we created a new benchmark, CellTrack-Bench, which assesses Vision-Language Models' (VLMs) cell-tracking-related performance against specialized trackers. The full benchmark draws from 15 standard cell-tracking datasets across four imaging modalities and comprises 1,537 problems corresponding to 9,041 cell-linking decisions. We selected a hard subset requiring greater reasoning effort by identifying failures shared across distinct algorithmic trackers. With this proposed dataset, we: (i) evaluated different environment harnesses for VLMs; (ii) benchmarked 9 frontier closed-source models and 13 open-weight models; and (iii) provided a detailed analysis of their failure modes. Code, the stored model outputs, and a pipeline that regenerates the benchmark from the source datasets are available at https://github.com/royerlab/celltrack-bench.
items.title: CellTrack-Bench: Microscopic Cell Tracking Benchmark for Vision-Language Models

items.summary: Multilingual language models can give different identity judgments when the same people's names are written in different scripts. We study this effect using 601 audited identity pairs with attested Devanagari and Latin forms, holding the question and relation fixed. Qwen2.5-7B's same-person accuracy falls from 35.1% in Latin to 8.5% in Devanagari under Marathi prompts, while different-person accuracy remains above 98%. Evaluation across five models reveals distinct response biases, and reduced tokenization fragmentation does not reliably close the gap. Replicating the design on 374 audited Malayalam pairs built from the same entities reproduces the effect in a second script and language family: same-person accuracy falls to 5.3%, about half the matched Devanagari rate, while the margin still ranks matching above non-matching names at 0.925 AUROC. Latin-trained probes recover label information from Devanagari states, exceeding a string-feature baseline under similarity-matched negatives. Scalar calibration recovers 87% of the raw model-probe balanced-accuracy gap, identifying decision criterion placement as a major contributor. Activation patching localises causal sensitivity to the second entity in Qwen's middle layers; one shared sensitivity direction transfers about half the full-state margin correction. A fact-independent intervention at this site raises held-out Marathi same-person accuracy from 6.5% to 33.5%, with 98.5% different-person accuracy. Together, these results distinguish script-dependent discrimination from criterion placement and identify a causal site for improving identity judgments.
items.title: Same Entity, Different Script: Diagnosing Cross-Script Entity Matching Failures in Language Models

items.summary: Large language models can repeat an instruction while failing to keep obeying it. We study this recall-compliance dissociation in long-horizon dialogue and define State Integrity Collapse: a model preserves a stated constraint in memory but stops applying it to later turns. We introduce StateTrack-Bench, a controlled suite of conversations covering numerical, format, role/persona, factual-memory, and logical-rule constraints. Across seven provider-pinned model snapshots and five dialogue-depth probes, strict joint retention ranges from 62.4% to 100.0%, with degradation concentrated in symbolic constraints and in one especially brittle model. A forked recall audit shows that 88.6% of observed failures are behavioral-drift failures rather than ordinary forgetting; excluding the brittle outlier preserves this diagnosis (84.4% of failures). Extended evaluations at depths up to 50 turns confirm that the dissociation persists beyond the core benchmark, while Structured State Anchoring recovers up to 24.4 points on immutable constraints. The results show that reliability cannot be inferred from single-turn instruction following alone; evaluation must track whether remembered constraints remain operational as dialogue state grows. Code and artifacts are available at: https://github.com/xzzvsxd/StateTrack.
items.title: When LLMs Forget What They Believe: Characterizing State Integrity Collapse in Long-Horizon Dialogues

items.summary: Low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites are vital in providing seamless connectivities to ground users (GUs). However, complex satellite-to-ground propagation and non-negligible satellite failure probabilities make single-satellite transmission unreliable. To address this issue, we consider a multi-LEO-satellite communication network (mLEO-CN), where a typical GU is served by multiple LEO satellites. The satellite locations are modeled as a binomial point process on a sphere and ordered according to their distances to the GU. To improve communication reliability, a serial communication scheme is adopted, in which the subsequent satellite is activated only when all preceding satellites fail to satisfy the target signal-to-noise ratio threshold. By employing the tool of stochastic geometry, we derive key performance metrics, including overall transmission success probability, average transmission rate, and end-to-end delay under the serial communication scheme by incorporating both shadowed Rician (SR) fading and satellite failure probabilities. To improve analytical tractability, we derive asymptotic expressions for the end-to-end transmission success probability in two special cases by leveraging the asymptotic expression of the SR fading model and a Gamma-distribution, and further propose a cluster-based approximation approach for the overall transmission success probability. Building on these analyses, we formulate an optimization problem to maximize the ratio of the overall transmission success probability to the end-to-end delay, and obtain its solution using a one-dimensional search approach. Numerical results validate the analysis, reveal the impact of key parameters, and identify the optimal number of serving LEO satellites under different constellation altitudes.
items.title: Stochastic Geometry Analysis and Optimization for Multi-LEO Satellite-Assisted Communications

items.summary: We study intermediate sample-size efficiency for censored regression tests when the signal and significance level both tend to zero. Independent treatment assignment permits finite-sample conditional sign calibration under arbitrary outcome dependence. For stationary ergodic latent fields with independent smooth site noise, bounded scores learned from the same pooled outcomes retain their first-order drift under empirical squared-error consistency, without an estimation-rate requirement. An observable censored rank procedure consequently admits an explicit leading cost on long-range dependent fields with nonsummable covariances. Smooth response scores admit a complementary result without independent site noise. For observational fields, separated blocks and paired variance calibration control the dependence approximation at the nominal testing level and yield sample-size costs under explicit absolute-regularity envelopes. An exactly centered censored contrast removes unknown marginal centering under stated exogeneity conditions. We also give a product-limit construction for independent random censoring, information-loss identities, and directional score-bank comparisons. Numerical studies distinguish procedure loss, score-learning loss, and spatial variance inflation. A stationary nonergodic counterexample and an uncensored Gaussian benchmark delimit the field results. Independent-data proofs, finite-range constructions, and a finite-dimensional measurement extension are included in the same manuscript.
tags: censored regression; intermediate efficiency; long-range dependence; random field; randomization tes
items.title: Intermediate efficiency of censored regression tests on stationary random fields

items.summary: Background : The rapid digitisation of allied health education has led to an alarming rise in Digital Eye Strain (DES), also termed Computer Vision Syndrome (CVS), among undergraduate Bachelor of Physiotherapy (BPT) students. Standard therapies like artificial tears provide temporary lubrication without resolving the underlying neuro-vascular tension and oxidative ocular stress. Objectives : To evaluate and compare the therapeutic efficacy of daily Isotonic Saline Jal Neti versus Sterile Triphala Water Eye Wash over 4 weeks on digital asthenopia, tear film stability, tear volume, and visual comfort in a cohort of 16 BPT students. Methodology : A 4-week prospective, parallel-group, randomized controlled empirical pilot trial was conducted at Maya Devi University, Dehradun. Sixteen BPT students (aged 18–25) meeting inclusion criteria (screen time ≥ 6 hrs/day, CVS-Q ≥ 6, TBUT < 10 s) were randomized 1:1 into Group A (Jal Neti, n=8) and Group B (Sterile Triphala Water Eye Wash, n=8). Outcome metrics assessed at baseline (Day 0) and post-intervention (Day 28) included: Computer Vision Syndrome Questionnaire (CVS-Q), Visual Fatigue Scale (VFS, 0-60), Tear Break-Up Time (TBUT, seconds), and Schirmer’s Test-I (mm/5 min). Results : Both groups exhibited statistically significant intra-group improvements across all parameters (p < 0.001). Group B (Triphala) achieved superior improvement in tear film stability and lacrimal secretion: TBUT increased by +4.15 ± 0.80 s in Group B vs. +2.30 ± 0.60 s in Group A (p < 0.001); Schirmer-I values increased by +4.85 ± 1.10 mm in Group B vs. +2.65 ± 0.85 mm in Group A (p < 0.001). Conversely, Group A (Jal Neti) achieved greater relief from central visual fatigue and periocular headaches: VFS scores decreased by -18.60 ± 2.95 points in Group A vs. -14.25 ± 2.75 points in Group B (p < 0.01). Total CVS-Q scores dropped markedly in both groups (Group A: 12.75 to 5.25; Group B: 13.00 to 4.90). Conclusion : Both modalities significantly alleviate digital eye strain in BPT students. Sterile Triphala eye wash is particularly potent for restoring ocular surface hydration and tear film stability, whereas Jal Neti excels in alleviating deep neuromuscular fatigue and periorbital strain.
tags: Digital Eye Strain, Jal Neti, Triphala, Tear Break-Up Time, Schirmer's Test, Physiotherapy Students,
items.title: Comparative Evaluation of Isotonic Saline Jal Neti versus Sterile Triphala Water Eye Wash on Digital Asthenopia, Tear Film Dynamics, and Visual Comfort in Undergraduate Physiotherapy Students: A Single-Center Empirical Pilot Study

items.summary: Despite significant advances in deep learning-based failure prognosis, existing predictive maintenance frameworks consistently terminate at the prediction step, leaving the critical operational challenge of prioritising maintenance resources across heterogeneous asset fleets unresolved. This paper addresses this gap by proposing an integrated framework that couples Long Short-Term Memory network-based Remaining Useful Life prediction with the Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution for data-driven multi-criteria maintenance scheduling, validated on the NASA C-MAPSS FD001 turbofan degradation benchmark. The framework dynamically synthesises predicted health indicators with operational criteria encompassing machine criticality, maintenance cost, and production downtime impact to generate a ranked intervention schedule whose quality is evaluated through a rigorous, assumption-free protocol comprising precision-recall analysis, area under the precision-recall curve, Spearman rank correlation, and a scheduling efficiency ratio against a random baseline. A five-seed ablation study comparing Long Short-Term Memory, Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory, and Gated Recurrent Unit architectures, with Wilcoxon signed-rank validation, establishes statistically equivalent prediction accuracy, confirming the architecture-agnostic nature of the scheduling design.
items.title: Code and analysis: A Deep Learning and TOPSIS Framework for Predictive Maintenance Scheduling in Smart Manufacturing: An Industry 4.0 Approach

items.summary: Coordinating two players in a cooking task requires a vision-language agent to track changing scene states, sequence recipe steps, and allocate shared resources under a time budget. We introduce an Overcooked-inspired benchmark for evaluating these capabilities in Unreal Engine environments constructed using coding agents. A single vision-language model controls both players from top-down visual observations, selecting high-level actions while the engine executes navigation. The benchmark contains 20 maps in five categories. These categories support evaluation of centralized coordination under equipment contention, changing terrain, and handoff dependencies. A prop legend and pot ingredient-count indicators provide explicit visual cues, while grid-based destinations support spatial grounding. The evaluation compares four VLMs on all 20 maps, measuring task score, order completion, delivery precision, action acceptance rate, and model API expenditure. A memory ablation on the same 20 maps examines the effect of a shared, self-authored notebook while retaining six-response action history in both conditions. The strongest evaluated model, \texttt{gpt-6-astra}, achieves 26.2\% mean order completion. Notebook memory has mixed score effects across models, with positive mean differences for Claude and Qwen and negative differences for GPT and Gemini.
items.title: DuoCook: An Overcooked-Inspired Benchmark for Visual Planning and Coordination

items.summary: Large language models can repeat an instruction while failing to keep obeying it. We study this recall-compliance dissociation in long-horizon dialogue and define State Integrity Collapse: a model preserves a stated constraint in memory but stops applying it to later turns. We introduce StateTrack-Bench, a controlled suite of conversations covering numerical, format, role/persona, factual-memory, and logical-rule constraints. Across seven provider-pinned model snapshots and five dialogue-depth probes, strict joint retention ranges from 62.4% to 100.0%, with degradation concentrated in symbolic constraints and in one especially brittle model. A forked recall audit shows that 88.6% of observed failures are behavioral-drift failures rather than ordinary forgetting; excluding the brittle outlier preserves this diagnosis (84.4% of failures). Extended evaluations at depths up to 50 turns confirm that the dissociation persists beyond the core benchmark, while Structured State Anchoring recovers up to 24.4 points on immutable constraints. The results show that reliability cannot be inferred from single-turn instruction following alone; evaluation must track whether remembered constraints remain operational as dialogue state grows. Code and artifacts are available at: https://github.com/xzzvsxd/StateTrack.
items.title: When LLMs Forget What They Believe: Characterizing State Integrity Collapse in Long-Horizon Dialogues

items.summary: Recent advances in search agents have enabled large language models to tackle complex tasks by retrieving and synthesizing external information. However, existing search agents often lack search-state awareness, i.e., the ability to recognize what information has been obtained and what remains missing, leading to hallucinated reasoning and prematurely terminated search. To address this limitation, we propose Self-Assessment Reinforcement Learning (SARL), a reinforcement learning framework in which models learn to recognize their own search state during training and improve their search behavior accordingly, without requiring additional assessment at test time. SARL achieves this through a dual reward design that captures the corrective effect of each assessment while penalizing excessive reliance on it, jointly encouraging effective and efficient search trajectories. Under this setup, SARL achieves a 24.3% relative improvement over the strongest baseline, with average gains of 35.9% on multi-hop reasoning and 27.9% on deep research benchmarks against the strongest per-benchmark baselines. SARL further surpasses methods built on auxiliary supervision or multi-agent coordination, despite operating as a standalone RL framework with no inference-time scaffolding. Beyond final performance, SARL maintains training stability under extended search horizons, a regime where existing methods consistently degrade, enabling sustained gains as task complexity grows.
items.title: Self-Assessment Reinforcement Learning for Search-State Awareness in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models

items.summary: Humanoid loco-manipulation in dynamic scenes is non-Markovian: cues vanish as objects change or are hidden, or leave the view as the robot turns and walks, yet whole-body vision-language-action (VLA) policies see only the present. We present WholeBodyMem, an object-guided perceptual memory that keeps the pre-history of object events seen before the robot acts on its goal. SAM3 tracks the task objects, and their events causally select key frames within an adaptive budget, which the action expert reads by cross-attention together with object tokens encoding appearance, geometry and time. We also contribute HuMeGo, a humanoid memory benchmark with six simulated and six real-world Unitree G1 tasks. Keeping the right frames rather than more frames, WholeBodyMem surpasses memoryless and uniform-memory baselines, raising its base policy's success from 29.1% to 72.6% in simulation and from 36.7% to 88.3% on the real robot, while also improving the standard SIMPLE tasks (70.2% to 86.9%).
items.title: Memory before Goal: Role of Pre-History Memory for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

items.summary: Scaling embedding capacity alongside Transformer computation is an emerging trend in language models. This trend makes high compression rates increasingly useful. Hence, we study extreme compression of Per-Layer Embeddings (PLE), which follow this trend and account for 35.2% of the parameters of Gemma 4 E4B. At such rates, conventional quantizers give each token-layer vector its own code of only a few bytes. We instead develop OPTIC (Output-Path-fitted, Token-shared Indexed Codes), which stores one quantized code tuple per token and decodes it at every layer with a layer-specific affine decoder. Codes and decoders are fitted to the PLE output path rather than to the stored vectors. At about $100\times$ PLE compression of bfloat16 (BF16) E4B, OPTIC retains an aggregate 97.8% of the uncompressed model's performance across seven benchmarks, whereas product quantization, the strongest of six conventional baselines, retains 66.3%. At $594\times$ and $1,002\times$ PLE compression of BF16 E4B, OPTIC retains 90.5% and 84.1%. On the official E4B release with 4-bit linear weights and 16-bit activations (W4A16), OPTIC retains 96.9% at about $100\times$ PLE compression. During inference at about $100\times$ PLE compression, BF16 E4B uses 29.7% less GPU memory than with uncompressed PLE at the same key-value cache size, while running at most 0.40% slower.
items.title: Extreme Compression of Per-Layer Embeddings via Cross-Layer Latent Vector Quantization

items.summary: Every LLM request SWAN AI-SQL (https://github.com/ZhaoFuheng/SWAN-AISQL) and the baselines issue on SemBench MOVIE/ECOMM/MMQA, the 30-query hybrid bench of the PLOP paper and the SWAN 2.0 benchmark (https://github.com/ZhaoFuheng/SWANBench), with the provider's answer, its measured latency and its cost, as a DuckDB file (gzip-compressed, 0.96 GB; 4.4 GB unpacked; 2,409,502 recorded calls) for the repository's cache proxy (serve/ai_cache_server.py). It holds SWAN AI-SQL, LOTUS 1.2.4, PLOP (the public Morrila fork, DP cost-model mode), BlendSQL 0.1.27, ThalamusDB 0.1.15 (exact mode) and Palimpzest 1.5.3 (Abacus optimizer) on every benchmark each of them runs. SWAN AI-SQL's recordings are its current ones (2026-10-23, DuckDB 2.0.0); every SWAN 2.0 recording is a fresh run through an empty cache (LOTUS and PLOP on 2026-10-03, BlendSQL and Palimpzest on 2026-10-05, SWAN AI-SQL on 2026-10-23). Always use the latest version: the concept DOI and serve/fetch_cache.sh resolve to it. Every table in the repositories replays without a provider key: run serve/fetch_cache.sh (it downloads, checks and unpacks the latest version), then the benchmark harnesses; the proxy replays each recorded answer with its recorded latency and cost. Model: gpt-5.6-luna, temperature 0, each system's default prompts (zero-shot). Replay matches requests byte for byte; an edited query, another model, or a client library that renders the request differently is a fresh request. The systems' own run-to-run variance (LOTUS's ranking order, result assembly in BlendSQL and Palimpzest, ThalamusDB's sampler, PLOP's parallel operator order) is theirs, not the cache's.
items.title: SWAN AI-SQL replay cache: recorded gpt-5.6-luna answers of SWAN, LOTUS, BlendSQL, Palimpzest, ThalamusDB and PLOP on SemBench, the PLOP hybrid bench and SWAN 2.0
